items.title: Strategic Focus – Healthy, Safe and Inclusive Communities
PDL-LEG-23-045, Amendment to Traffic and Parking By-law – Administrative Monetary Penalties
notes:
Graham Walsh, Regional Solicitor, provided an overview of the report, explaining that this would take parking infractions out of the Provincial Offences Court system, and move them to a more streamlined system, where a screening officer works with the person who has been given the ticket to either maintain the fine, reduce or remove it altogether. G. Walsh explained that the benefits of this approach are lower court costs, and that generally revenue increases as well. G. Walsh also confirmed that this has been done at the request of the cities of Cambridge, Kitchener, and Waterloo.

Responding to questions from the Committee, G. Walsh confirmed that there is always an audit to assess whether the system is running effectively. 

The Committee asked staff to report back with more information regarding the fine review process, including what the system currently is, and who are the parties involved.

items.title: Strategic Focus – Responsive and Engaging Public Service
EES-SAM-23-001, Asset Management and Capital Budget Alignment (Staff Presentation)
notes:
Jennifer Rose, Commissioner, Engineering and Environmental Services and Craig Dyer, Commissioner, Corporate Services/Chief Financial Officer provided a presentation on asset management and capital budget alignment, including an overview of the steps of bringing a capital plan together and funding gaps. C. Dyer explained that the goal is to not use long term borrowing to fund asset renewal works, and to preserve debt capacity by ensuring there is sufficient contributions to capital reserves in the long run. C. Dyer noted that the current strategy is working, as debt levels have remained the same over the past few years.

A copy of the presentation is attached to the minutes.

This report was received for information.

Responding to questions from the Committee, C. Dyer noted that the intention behind reserve funds are to make sure that they are sustainable in terms of their ability to fund the capital program, as capital investments are not the same year over year. C. Dyer noted that the goal is to have enough funds, so the Region does not need to issue debt.

In response to a question from the Committee, C. Dyer shared that with a few exceptions, there is no specific requirements in the Municipal Act that direct a level of reserve or reserve fund balance, and that municipalities are allowed to establish this target as deemed appropriate. J. Rose confirmed that the water reserve is mandated through the Safe Drinking Water Act.

items.title: Other Business
notes:
Responding to a question from the Committee, Mathieu Goetzke, Commissioner, Transportation Services stated that a new record of ridership was achieved on Thursday, September 7th, 2023, with approximately 134,000 riders on GRT and 20,000 on the LRT. M. Goetzke confirmed that staff are aware of the delays that occurred and that the root causes still need to be unpacked, which will help inform the work staff is doing for next year's budget, and that there may be a need for some operational changes.

Responding to a question from the Committee, C. Dyer explained that the provincial gas tax revenue is to a large extent, based on ridership, and to the extent that ridership is increasing in the Region at a faster rate than in other jurisdictions, that should result in additional provincial gas tax funding for the Region.  

Responding to questions from the Committee, M. Goetzke noted that the Region’s LRT has the highest performance in Ontario in terms of reliability, and that to support the increase in ridership, the first step would be to increase the frequency of vehicles before adding length to the cars, which would require purchases.

The Committee asked staff to share the positive GRT and LRT news to Council on a regular basis, in addition to the challenges, so that Council can get a feeling on how the system is working and moving across the Region.
